claim: The core capture principle: the easier note creation is, the less likely you are to lose ideas; recommends global hotkeys + app launchers as the desktop primitives.
quote: The easier it is to create notes, the less likely you are to lose an important idea.

claim: Obsidian's core Daily Notes plugin opens a note based on today's date, or creates it if missing, intended for journals, to-do lists, and daily logs.
quote: Daily notes... opens a note based on today's date, or creates it if it doesn't exist.

claim: Periodic Notes extends the core daily-note idea to weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly notes — the standard upgrade once daily notes are sticky.
quote: Create/manage your daily, weekly, and monthly notes in Obsidian.

claim: Template should evolve with use: if your template has more than 10 sections you'll dread opening it; consistency matters more than quality.
quote: If your template has more than 10 sections, you'll dread opening it... Consistency matters more than quality in daily capture.

claim: Community-shared minimal daily-note template uses Templater navigation links between previous/current/next day and depends on 'Trigger Templater on new file creation'.
quote: the Templater setting 'Trigger Templater on new file creation' must be activated

claim: QuickAdd is a widely-used Obsidian plugin combining templates, captures, macros, and multis behind single hotkeys.
quote: QuickAdd adds one fast command for repeatable Obsidian workflows.

claim: QuickAdd Capture choices write text to a target file from anywhere in Obsidian; targets can be dynamic dates, folders, tags, or the active file.
quote: A Capture allows you to quickly add content to predefined files... save it from anywhere in Obsidian, without leaving your current window setup.

claim: Templater adds date math, JavaScript commands, and folder-template triggers — required for any daily template beyond static text.
quote: A template plugin for obsidian.

claim: Mobile capture solutions bypass Obsidian's slow cold-start; on iOS Drafts is the canonical fast-capture frontend, on Android Fleeting Notes and Zettel Notes are the recommended companion apps.
quote: the best Quick Capture app I've ever used. It is lightning fast, powerful, flexible

claim: Community consensus: Obsidian Mobile is too slow to be the primary capture surface, so use a faster intermediary (Lumberjack URL scheme, third-party app) that sinks into the vault.
quote: Obsidian needs to load, the less it has to load and the faster the device is the faster it'll be, but you'll need to hang onto that thought.

claim: A self-contained iOS Shortcut pattern uses the obsidian://actions-uri/note/create scheme with URL-encoded vault + file + content to append captures to a dated note.
quote: obsidian://actions-uri/note/create?vault=$VAULT&file=$FILE&content=$TEXTBOX

claim: QuickAdd choices can be triggered from external apps via the obsidian://quickadd URI, which is what makes one-tap iOS Shortcut capture work.
quote: QuickAdd choices can be launched from external scripts or apps such as Shortcuts on Mac and iOS, through the use of the obsidian://quickadd URI.

claim: Newer iOS companion apps (Quick Draft for Obsidian, released into the App Store) bundle voice transcription and lock-screen capture without the Drafts learning curve.
quote: Quick Draft for Obsidian

claim: Interstitial journaling means writing brief timestamped notes between activities; in Obsidian a 'Notes' heading in the daily note plus a time-insert hotkey is enough.
quote: Interstitial journaling means writing brief, timestamped notes throughout your day

claim: The Interstitial Journal plugin adds one hotkey that stamps the current time before your cursor in the active note — the minimum useful tooling for the practice.
quote: A plugin for Obsidian that allows you to create interstitial journal entries.

claim: QuickAdd's author runs a Sunday weekly review that aggregates project mentions from daily notes; the system is designed so skipping days doesn't break the workflow.
quote: I use the Obsidian querying feature to extract information on the projects from my daily notes. Any mention of a project in a daily note is aggregated into the weekly review.

claim: Single-inbox.md pattern with end-of-day processing: capture everything to Inbox/inbox.md with optional prefixes, file/categorise in one evening pass.
quote: During the day, I dump everything into a single inbox file. No folders, no tags, no thinking. Then, at the end of the day, AI reads the inbox and files each entry.

claim: A Templater-driven archive/trash/move trio lets the inbox be processed like email: each command files the current note and opens the next.
quote: The script automatically opens the next note in the folder after the previous note has been processed

claim: Daily notes work best when they become the default hub — every workday touches the same note, which gives short-lived ideas a default home.
quote: Chaos to Clarity: Unleash Obsidian Daily Notes

claim: Nick Milo's Linking Your Thinking framework distinguishes fleeting notes from evergreen notes; daily notes are the canonical incubator for fleeting material.
quote: daily notes are often used as a place for 'interstitial journaling' – capturing and logging thoughts as they occur
